name: Brooklyn Bridge Automated Pedestrian Counts Demonstration Project (Historic)
description:
This dataset contains hourly automated pedestrian counts recorded on the Brooklyn Bridge as part of a demonstration project. Each row represents one hour and includes the timestamp, total pedestrian count, and separate counts for people walking toward Manhattan and toward Brooklyn. Weather conditions are included for each hour, covering a short weather summary (such as clear-day, cloudy, or partly-cloudy-night), temperature, and precipitation. The data also includes fixed latitude and longitude coordinates for the bridge and occasional notes on holidays or events, such as New Year's Eve, Labor Day, or Daylight Saving Time changes.

The data can be used to study pedestrian flow patterns by time of day, season, and weather, to compare travel demand in each direction across the bridge, and to examine how holidays and events affect foot traffic. The location fields support mapping and spatial visualization, while the directional counts and weather variables make the dataset useful for transportation planning, urban mobility research, and exploratory analysis of how conditions influence walking behavior.
